hero.greeting: Hello, my name is Pedro Vitor
hero.bio: I am a Computer Science student specializing in Data Science. I also study software engineering, software architecture, and system design, with the goal of eventually moving into MLOps.
hero.en_notice: Hello, and thanks for the visit. If you do not know portuguese, you can translate to english by clicking in the translate button on the menu.

rec_system.title: Recommender System
rec_system.desc: I implemented and evaluated two recommendation systems: a memory-based approach using KNN and a model-based approach using Funk's SVD. The pipeline involved dataset cleaning and organization, data normalization, model training, and performance evaluation. In the SVD-based approach, latent factors for users and items were learned to model their interactions. For both approaches, I performed hyperparameter tuning to optimize the models and compare their performance. The model achieved an RMSE of 0.8527 and a validation RMSE of 0.9313. The project includes a paper detailing the methodology, experiments, and results.

movie_rec.title: Movie Recommender System
movie_rec.desc: A simple movie recommendation system that, unlike the one described above, was built using the Scikit-learn library. The user selects the number of movies they wish to rate and assigns a score to each one. Based on this, the system recommends a list of movies the user is likely to enjoy. Two approaches were implemented: one using a "bag of words" (or "soup of words") technique and another that did not use this approach.

mini_course.title: Machine Learning Short Course
mini_course.desc: Planned and taught an introductory mini-course covering supervised learning concepts, including Linear Regression, Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, and Clustering. The course provided a practical and instructional overview of the entire machine learning pipeline—from preprocessing to model training and evaluation—using Python and Scikit-learn. The presentation was open to the general academic community.

lin_reg.title: Linear Regression
lin_reg.desc: Iterative development of a linear regression algorithm. The data is processed, ranging from missing value checks to numerical data normalization.

nn_class.title: Classification with Neural Networks
nn_class.desc: A dense neural network system trained to solve a classification problem. The project uses a classic problem: classifying Titanic survivors. The pipeline involved data cleaning and preparation, data normalization, training combined with validation, and techniques to prevent overfitting, such as dropout.

data_analysis.title: Data Analysis
data_analysis.desc: An exploratory data analysis (EDA) was conducted using data collected by the IBGE (Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics). The aim of the study was to perform data mining to uncover hidden insights, thereby enabling better attention to cases requiring it. Data preprocessing and clustering were carried out during the analysis to facilitate a more effective examination.

assoc_rules.title: Association Rules
assoc_rules.desc: This project was analyzed using a different approach, employing association rules, such as Support, Confidence, Lift, and Conviction, to explore and discover the events and characteristics that led customers to abandon a telephone company's service (i.e., to identify the factors driving churn). In addition to association rules, the FP-Growth algorithm was used to assist in the data analysis.

clustering.title: Clustering
clustering.desc: An analysis and clustering process was performed on a dataset regarding student performance at a school to identify student profiles and examine correlations. The goal was to determine whether measures should be implemented to assist students with poor performance. Preliminary data ETL was conducted, and PCA was applied to improve the visualization of the resulting groups. The K-prototypes algorithm was selected for clustering due to its ability to handle a mix of categorical and non-categorical data.

embedding_cluster.title: Embedding Cluster
embedding_cluster.desc: Experiment for semantic proximity with embeddings: sentences and adjectives are vectorized and grouped to reveal how language models organize meaning in latent space. Pipeline includes embedding generation, dimensionality reduction (PCA/UMAP), clustering and interactive visualization to validate prompt engineering hypotheses and textual similarity.

nn_linreg.title: Neural network for mathematical representations
nn_linreg.desc: These are the "simplest" ones. I developed two neural network implementations using PyTorch to understand how the network changes and learns when adjusting parameters such as layers, neurons, and epochs and how techniques to prevent overfitting, like dropout, alter the network. These two implementations were designed for linear regression and for modeling a sine wave.

rnn.title: Recurrent Neural Network
rnn.desc: In this project, we developed an image classifier using the CIFAR-10 dataset. For validation, I employed a holdout technique, splitting the data into 80% for training, 10% for testing, and 10% for validation. To mitigate overfitting, I applied data augmentation, performing image mirroring, rotation, and normalization during training.

encoders.title: Recurrent Neural Network (Encoders)
encoders.desc: On VAEs i created an anomaly detector. So the neural network learn how to tell the difference, between an image she recognizes and one she doesn't. For this one i got the fashionmnist dataset. Again i used holdout for separate the dataset 80/10/10. The model compression is from 748 to 32 dimensions.

lstm.title: LSTM Neural Network
lstm.desc: On LSTM i desing a price estimator for bitcoin price. I used the bitcoin historic price change, but i only took data from 2023 onwards. Why? Because my experiment was taking more than 6 hours to complete. And yes using the VGA on google colab. I normalizes the atributes using the z-score, because is (as far as I know) the best way to normalize without experiencing significant fluctuations in the data's means and standard deviations, and without the data being influenced by extreme variations.

f1_vrum.title: F1 vrum-vrum
f1_vrum.desc: An API built using FastAPI. The project aims to create an API featuring Formula 1 season data. It will allow users to query drivers, teams, circuits, races, seasons, and results. Planned future features include predictions, statistics, and a dashboard.

ecommerce.title: Gaming E-commerce
ecommerce.desc: I built a full-stack e-commerce platform using AdonisJS, which runs on Node.js. The platform is a game store following the MVC pattern that supports various platforms ranging from PC to PS5. The backend was built as a REST API featuring authentication, session management, and database management (using SQLite). Database operations were handled via an ORM (including migrations and seeders), and the RAWG API was used to populate the data. Project features include CRUD functionality for users and items (with an admin dashboard), a wishlist, and a commenting system. Additionally, the project implements debouncing and pagination for database queries, shopping cart persistence, and integration with the Stripe payment gateway.

hub_alunos.title: Student HUB
hub_alunos.desc: Collaborative platform to connect students: material sharing by subject, Q&A forums, event board and mentorship system. Built with Next.js App Router, RBAC auth, Prisma + Postgres, Zod validation and mobile-first design.

refatoracao_extensao.title: Extension Project Refactoring
refatoracao_extensao.desc: Legacy university extension system modernization via Strangler Fig: from coupled monolith to Clean Architecture with SOLID, dependency inversion, test suite (18% → 74% coverage), Docker and CI/CD — cutting deploy from 45min to 6min.

comp_prog.title: Competitive Programming & Algorithms
comp_prog.desc: Refers to my study and projects focused on algorithms, which led me to prepare for programming marathons. Also includes solutions for several LeetCode problems.

research.title: LLMs, economics and BigFive
research.desc: For my capstone project, I conducted research integrating Computer science, economics, and psychology. The goal was to use LLMs to simulate decision-making and analyze their strategies, specifically examining how variations across the Big Five personality spectrum and macroeconomic contexts influence those decisions.

about_me.title: A Little About Me
about_me.subtitle: A Little About My Learning Journey
about_me.desc: During university, I began my studies with C. Later, while studying OOP, I learned core concepts using JAVA, covering polymorphism, inheritance, and encapsulation. I also studied C++ for competitive programming. As shown in the portfolio, I have used TypeScript to build an e-commerce with NodeJS (using agents). Currently, I am focusing more on Python, Golang, and SQL—practicing hands-on skills, modeling, and queries—to pursue my desired career path in Data Science / MLOps. I use Linux on my laptop for programming and learning, including Docker, terminal usage, and more. During college, I also focused my studies on artificial intelligence, covering subjects such as AI, machine learning, data mining, neural networks, natural language processing, and recommendation systems. Now, I am exploring a different area: software engineering and architecture. To finish, i'm studying system desing.

contact.title: Get in Touch
contact.desc: I am available for new opportunities and collaborations.

sistema_recomendacao.title: Recommender System
sistema_recomendacao.subtitle: This project involved the implementation and evaluation of two memory-based KNN approaches, specifically item-based and user-based. As well as Funk's SVD (a model-based approach). The workflow encompassed the entire pipeline, including data cleaning, normalization, denormalization, and validation. Hyperparameter tuning was performed during the experiment to evaluate and identify the best-performing approach, and a technical article was produced to detail the project.
sistema_recomendacao.about_p1: This project implements and compares two classic paradigms: memory-based CF (KNN) and model-based (Funk SVD). The goal was to understand trade-offs in complexity, interpretability and rating prediction accuracy.
sistema_recomendacao.about_p2: The full pipeline covered cleaning and organizing the dataset, normalization, train/validation/test split, training and evaluation. For SVD, latent factors for users and items were learned via regularized matrix factorization.
sistema_recomendacao.gallery_desc: Replace the images below with your charts: loss curve, rating distribution and RMSE comparison. Swap the SVGs in img/.
sistema_recomendacao.gallery_img1_caption: Graph representing the RMSE value in relation to the quantity of latent factors.
sistema_recomendacao.gallery_img2_caption: Graph representing the RMSE value in relation to the K values.
sistema_recomendacao.gallery_img3_caption: Figure 3 — RMSE comparison: KNN baseline vs tuned SVD.
sistema_recomendacao.method_p: Pipeline: Dataset → Cleaning → Normalization → Training (KNN/SVD) → Hyper-tuning → Evaluation (RMSE) → Paper. Paper covers cold-start, popularity bias and error analysis.
sistema_recomendacao.tech_p: Python, Pandas, Numpy, Scikit-learn, custom Funk SVD and Matplotlib for loss curves and rating distribution.
sistema_recomendacao.conclusion_p: SVD outperformed KNN (RMSE 0.8527 train / 0.9313 validation) at higher tuning cost. Foundation for hybrid and deep models.

sistema_recomendacao_filmes.title: Movie Recommender System
sistema_recomendacao_filmes.subtitle: Simple Scikit-learn recommender where users rate N movies and get personalized list. Two engineering approaches compared: with and without bag-of-words.
sistema_recomendacao_filmes.about_p1: Unlike the previous collaborative system, this is content-based. Flow: user rates movies, system computes similarity to suggest new titles.
sistema_recomendacao_filmes.about_p2: Two approaches were engineered: with bag-of-words — joining genres, cast/director and synopsis into a TF-IDF vector — and without BoW, using only structured metadata. Comparison shows textual context gain.
sistema_recomendacao_filmes.gallery_desc: Add here: sparse TF-IDF matrix, similarity heatmap and top-N ranking example. Replace SVGs in img/.
sistema_recomendacao_filmes.gallery_img1_caption: Figure 1 — Sparse TF-IDF matrix (terms vs movies).
sistema_recomendacao_filmes.gallery_img2_caption: Figure 2 — Cosine similarity heatmap between movies.
sistema_recomendacao_filmes.gallery_img3_caption: Figure 3 — Example top-5 recommendations after user rating.
sistema_recomendacao_filmes.method_p: TF-IDF vs One-hot, cosine / KNN (k=5) and ranking weighted by user rating. With BoW: more diverse and synopsis-sensitive.
sistema_recomendacao_filmes.tech_p: Python, Scikit-learn (CountVectorizer/TfidfVectorizer, cosine_similarity, NearestNeighbors), Pandas, Numpy. Interactive notebook with rating widgets.
sistema_recomendacao_filmes.conclusion_p: Bag-of-words brought more diversity and contextual relevance. Didactic project before moving to neural models.

mini_curso.title: Machine Learning Short Course
mini_curso.subtitle: Designed and taught an introductory course open to the academic community: full ML pipeline from scratch to didactic deployment.
mini_curso.about_p1: Course designed and taught by me, open to the community, with hands-on focus. Covered supervised learning — Linear Regression, Logistic Regression, Decision Trees — and clustering intro.
mini_curso.about_p2: Differentiator was showing the whole pipeline: data understanding → preprocessing → training → evaluation (metrics, confusion matrix, ROC) → overfitting/underfitting — all in Python with Scikit-learn.
mini_curso.gallery_desc: Insert slide screenshots, class photos and metric charts used in class.
mini_curso.gallery_img2_caption: Figure 2 — Open class for the academic community.
mini_curso.gallery_img3_caption: Figure 3 — Example confusion matrix and ROC curve in class.
mini_curso.method_p: 5 modules: Fundamentals, Regression, Classification, Clustering and Best practices (cross-validation, normalization, Pipeline and GridSearchCV).
mini_curso.tech_p: Python, Scikit-learn, Matplotlib, Pandas. Line-by-line commented notebooks, slides and exercises.
mini_curso.conclusion_p: Feedback highlighted clarity on bias-variance and live demo of sklearn Pipeline. Public repo with all materials.

regressao_linear.title: Linear Regression
regressao_linear.subtitle: Iterative development of linear regression — from missing-value handling to normalization — with custom implementation validated against Scikit-learn.
regressao_linear.about_p1: Iterative (gradient descent) implementation of linear regression, without using the closed-form solver first. Focus was mastering preprocessing: missing values, outliers, categorical encoding and normalization (MinMax / Z-score) for stable convergence.
regressao_linear.about_p2: Compared my implementation with sklearn's LinearRegression validating coefficients, cost (MSE) and learning curve per epoch.
regressao_linear.gallery_desc: Add GD convergence, fitted line and residual plot.
regressao_linear.gallery_img2_caption: Figure 2 — Fitted line vs actual points.
regressao_linear.gallery_img3_caption: Figure 3 — Residuals vs prediction for diagnostics.
regressao_linear.method_p: ETL with imputation, StandardScaler, GD (lr=0.01, 1000 epochs, early stopping) and evaluation via MSE, RMSE, R² + residual plot.
regressao_linear.tech_p: Python, Numpy, Pandas, Matplotlib, Scikit-learn for validation.
regressao_linear.conclusion_p: Normalization was crucial for stable GD. Custom implementation solidified understanding before using ready solvers.

analise_ibge.title: Data Analysis - IBGE
analise_ibge.subtitle: Full EDA on IBGE data to mine hidden patterns and cluster to prioritize attention to critical cases.
analise_ibge.about_p1: Using public IBGE microdata, I performed an end-to-end Exploratory Data Analysis: dictionary understanding, inconsistency handling, imputation, normalization and correlation visualization to mine hidden insights.
analise_ibge.about_p2: Second phase was clustering to group similar profiles, enabling segmented reading instead of overall average.
analise_ibge.gallery_desc: Replace with: correlation heatmap, regional histograms and cluster PCA.
analise_ibge.gallery_img1_caption: Figure 1 — Correlation heatmap across IBGE variables.
analise_ibge.gallery_img2_caption: Figure 2 — Distributions by region and income bracket.
analise_ibge.method_p: Cleaning (IQR), EDA (heatmap, pairplot, boxplots), K-Means with elbow/silhouette and cluster profiling for actionable recommendations.
analise_ibge.conclusion_p: Clustering revealed priority segments, guiding attention where most needed instead of generic policies.

regras_associacao.title: Association Rules
regras_associacao.subtitle: Discovering churn-driving patterns in telecom using Support, Confidence, Lift, Conviction and FP-Growth.
regras_associacao.about_p1: Instead of traditional EDA, analysis was guided by association rules to discover attribute combinations preceding churn. Metrics like Support, Confidence, Lift and Conviction filtered relevant rules.
regras_associacao.about_p2: FP-Growth (via mlxtend) accelerated frequent itemset mining vs Apriori, allowing multiple support thresholds.
regras_associacao.gallery_desc: Include rule graph, top frequent itemsets and lift vs confidence scatter.
regras_associacao.gallery_img1_caption: Figure 1 — Antecedent → consequent graph (size = support, color = lift).
regras_associacao.gallery_img2_caption: Figure 2 — Top-10 frequent itemsets by support.
regras_associacao.gallery_img3_caption: Figure 3 — Scatter Lift vs Confidence of filtered rules.
regras_associacao.method_p: One-hot → FP-Growth (min_support=0.05) → rules (min_confidence=0.3) → filter Lift>1.2 and Conviction>1.1 → ranking.
regras_associacao.conclusion_p: Rules like {Monthly Contract, No Partner} → {Churn} with Lift 1.56 highlight risk profiles for proactive action.

clustering.title: Clustering - Student Performance
clustering.subtitle: Analysis and clustering of student profiles to identify correlations and propose pedagogical interventions. ETL + PCA + K-Prototypes.
clustering.about_p1: Student performance dataset with numerical (grades, attendance, study hours) and categorical (shift, parental education, method) attributes. Goal was to discover profiles and correlations to act where performance is low.
clustering.about_p2: Differentiator was K-Prototypes — K-Means extension handling mixed variables — instead of dropping categoricals. PCA only for 2D visualization.
clustering.gallery_desc: Add PCA 2D, radar per cluster and silhouette.
clustering.gallery_img1_caption: Figure 1 — Clusters projected in 2D via PCA.
clustering.gallery_img2_caption: Figure 2 — Radar with avg grades, attendance and hours per cluster.
clustering.gallery_img3_caption: Figure 3 — Elbow + silhouette for choosing k.
clustering.method_p: ETL with Z-score, k selection (3..6), K-Prototypes with tuned gamma and PCA + radar visualization.
clustering.tech_p: Python, Pandas, K-Prototypes, KModes, Scikit-learn, Matplotlib.
clustering.conclusion_p: Clusters revealed 'high attendance low grade' vs 'low attendance medium grade', guiding specific interventions.

embedding_cluster.title: Embedding Cluster
embedding_cluster.subtitle: Semantic proximity of sentences and adjectives in latent space, for studies involving LLMs.
embedding_cluster.about_p1: The project involves clustering based on semantic similarity. During my capstone project, I proposed an approach to a problem I was investigating for my experiments: combining prompting, psychology, and similarity. I wondered: why not use embeddings to measure the proximity between the phrases and the adjectives?
embedding_cluster.about_p2: These phrases and adjectives relate to the personality model proposed by Goldberg in his study, with the phrases drawn from the dataset used by the IPIP. I then generated embeddings for all these texts and measured the similarity between the phrases and the adjectives.
embedding_cluster.gallery_desc: Replace with your charts: UMAP 2D of embeddings, cosine similarity heatmap and dendrogram/hierarchy of clusters.
embedding_cluster.gallery_img1_caption: Figure 1 — 2D UMAP: sentences and adjectives colored by cluster. Proximity = semantic similarity.
embedding_cluster.gallery_img2_caption: Figure 2 — Cosine similarity heatmap between sentence/adjective pairs.
embedding_cluster.gallery_img3_caption: Figure 3 — Elbow + silhouette for choosing k and cluster stability.
embedding_cluster.method_p: 1) Curation of sentences/adjectives, 2) Vectorization with Sentence-Transformers, 3) L2 normalization + cosine similarity, 4) Clustering (K-Means/HDBSCAN), 5) UMAP/PCA projection to 2D, 6) Qualitative prompt validation with LLMs.
embedding_cluster.tech_p: Python, Sentence-Transformers, Hugging Face, Scikit-learn, UMAP, Pandas, Numpy, Matplotlib/Plotly.
embedding_cluster.conclusion_p: Foundation for data-driven prompt engineering: picking adjectives that actually shift the embedding, measuring semantic drift between paraphrases and building similarity test suites for LLMs before production.

rede_matematica.title: Neural Network for Mathematical Representations
rede_matematica.subtitle: Two didactic PyTorch implementations to understand how layers, neurons, epochs and dropout affect learning — on linear regression and sine wave.
rede_matematica.about_p1: Simplest yet essential projects: two dense nets to approximate math functions. One learns y = ax + b and the other y = sin(x). Goal: observe architecture behavior varying depth, width, epochs and dropout.
rede_matematica.about_p2: Experiments showed direct impact of dropout on generalization and depth on curvature capture.
rede_matematica.gallery_desc: Include prediction vs ground-truth for sine, loss curve and dropout effect.
rede_matematica.gallery_img1_caption: Figure 1 — Network prediction vs true line y=ax+b.
rede_matematica.gallery_img2_caption: Figure 2 — Shallow vs deep net approximating sin(x).
rede_matematica.gallery_img3_caption: Figure 3 — With dropout 0.2: smoothed curve and better generalization.
rede_matematica.method_p: 1 layer (8 neurons) vs 4 layers (32), 50/500/2000 epochs, dropout 0.2. MSELoss, Adam.
rede_matematica.tech_p: Python, PyTorch, Numpy, Matplotlib. Net with Sequential, Linear, ReLU, Dropout.
rede_matematica.conclusion_p: Depth helps curvature but requires regularization. Didactic base for larger nets.

classificacao_titanic.title: Classification with Neural Networks
classificacao_titanic.subtitle: Dense net for classic Titanic — who survives? Pipeline: cleaning, normalization, validation and dropout against overfitting.
classificacao_titanic.about_p1: Dense neural net (MLP) for binary classification on Titanic. Classic task requiring good feature engineering: Age imputation, Sex/Embarked encoding, title extraction (Mr/Mrs) and FamilySize.
classificacao_titanic.about_p2: Training with holdout, StandardScaler and dropout (0.3) to avoid overfitting on small dataset.
classificacao_titanic.gallery_desc: Confusion matrix, ROC curve and accuracy curve.
classificacao_titanic.gallery_img3_caption: Figure 3 — Train vs validation accuracy per epoch.
classificacao_titanic.method_p: Input 8 feats → Dense 64 ReLU + Dropout 0.3 → Dense 32 ReLU + Dropout 0.3 → Sigmoid. Binary Crossentropy, Adam lr=0.001.
classificacao_titanic.conclusion_p: Accuracy ~0.80+, dropout reduced train-val gap from 0.12 to 0.04.

cifar10.title: CIFAR-10 Image Classifier
cifar10.subtitle: PyTorch CNN to classify 10 CIFAR-10 classes. Holdout 80/10/10 and data augmentation (flip, rotation, normalization) against overfitting.
cifar10.about_p1: Convolutional classifier (CNN) for CIFAR-10 (60k 32x32 images in 10 classes). Focus was mastering data augmentation and holdout for generalization.
cifar10.about_p2: Split: 80% train, 10% val, 10% test. Augmentation only on train: RandomHorizontalFlip, RandomRotation(15) and Normalize.
cifar10.gallery_desc: CIFAR-10 samples, augmentation and confusion matrix.
cifar10.gallery_img3_caption: Figure 3 — Confusion matrix: cat vs dog, plane vs bird.
cifar10.method_p: Conv 32→64→128, MaxPool, FC 512→128→10 with Dropout 0.5. Adam + StepLR.
cifar10.conclusion_p: Augmentation lifted accuracy by ~8-10 pp vs baseline.

vae.title: Autoencoders for Anomaly Detection
vae.subtitle: VAE trained on Fashion-MNIST as detector: learns to distinguish known vs anomaly. Compression 784 → 32 dims.
vae.about_p1: Goal was to vary VAE architecture to improve anomaly detection. Train only on 'normal' Fashion-MNIST classes; anomalies are unseen classes. Reconstruction error + KL divergence is anomaly score.
vae.about_p2: Compression: 784 → 32 dims in latent space, forcing compact manifold learning.
vae.gallery_desc: Normal vs anomaly reconstruction, latent space and AUROC curve.
vae.gallery_img2_caption: Figure 2 — High reconstruction error on anomalous class.
vae.method_p: Encoder 784→400→mu/logvar(32), reparameterization, Decoder 32→400→784, BCE+KL loss. Holdout 80/10/10.
vae.conclusion_p: Latent 16/32/64 and beta-VAE affect AUROC. 32 dims was best trade-off.

lstm.title: LSTM for Bitcoin
lstm.subtitle: Bitcoin price estimator with LSTM using history since 2023, Z-score normalization and 6h+ GPU training on Colab.
lstm.about_p1: LSTM to estimate BTC closing price using 30-day sliding window. Data cut from 2023 to make experiments feasible (full train >6h on Colab GPU). Features: Open, High, Low, Close, Volume.
lstm.about_p2: Z-score normalization (mean 0, std 1) chosen for robustness to crypto extremes vs MinMax, avoiding mean/std distortion.
lstm.gallery_desc: BTC series, sliding window and prediction vs actual.
lstm.gallery_img3_caption: Figure 3 — LSTM prediction vs actual price (validation).
lstm.method_p: API collection, Z-score fit on train, 30-day sequences, 2-layer LSTM hidden 50 + Dense 1, Adam MSE, 100 epochs, dropout 0.2.
lstm.conclusion_p: LAG in high volatility; baseline to evolve to Transformer/GRU and exogenous features (sentiment, macro).

f1_vrum.title: F1 Vrum-Vrum
f1_vrum.subtitle: REST API in FastAPI to query complete Formula 1 season data — drivers, teams, circuits, races and results. Base for stats, predictions and dashboard.
f1_vrum.about_p1: F1 Vrum-Vrum is a REST API built with FastAPI to centralize and expose historical and current Formula 1 data. Idea came from lack of well-structured open APIs with complete relational data (drivers ↔ teams ↔ seasons ↔ races ↔ results).
f1_vrum.about_p2: API allows querying Drivers, Teams, Circuits, Races, Seasons and Results normalized, via SQLAlchemy ORM and Postgres. Runs with Docker.
f1_vrum.gallery_desc: ER diagram, Swagger UI and JSON response example.
f1_vrum.gallery_img1_caption: Figure 1 — Relational model: Drivers, Teams, Circuits, Races.
f1_vrum.method_p: FastAPI + SQLAlchemy + Postgres + Docker. Routers, Pydantic schemas, models and services. Migrations and strong typing.
f1_vrum.tech_p: FastAPI, Python 3.11+, SQLAlchemy 2.0, PostgreSQL, Docker/Compose, Pydantic, Uvicorn.
f1_vrum.conclusion_p: Next: predictions, stats, dashboard, Redis cache, pagination, pytest and CI.

hub_alunos.title: Student HUB
hub_alunos.subtitle: Collaborative platform to connect students: material sharing, Q&A forums, event board and mentorship system.
hub_alunos.about_p1: The Student HUB was born to centralize academic life outside the official system. Instead of scattered WhatsApp groups, the platform gathers materials by subject, Q&A forums, event board and a mentorship system where seniors guide freshmen.
hub_alunos.about_p2: Architecture designed to scale: Next.js App Router with SSR for SEO, NextAuth auth, RBAC (student, tutor, coordinator), Prisma ORM with Postgres and PDF/image upload with validation. Focus on accessibility and mobile performance.
hub_alunos.gallery_desc: Screenshots: feed, subject page and profile.
hub_alunos.gallery_img1_caption: Figure 1 — Feed with materials and course filters.
hub_alunos.gallery_img2_caption: Figure 2 — Forum per subject with threads and solved marking.
hub_alunos.method_p: Monorepo with Next.js 14, Server Actions, Prisma + Postgres, Zod validation, Vitest tests, GitHub Actions CI and Vercel deploy. Cursor pagination on feed, cache with revalidateTag and Tailwind + shadcn design system.
hub_alunos.tech_p: Next.js, TypeScript, Prisma, PostgreSQL, NextAuth, Tailwind CSS, Zod, Vitest.
hub_alunos.conclusion_p: Realtime notifications, academic calendar integration and material recommendation via embeddings. Basis for System Design portfolio.

refatoracao_extensao.title: Extension Project Refactoring
refatoracao_extensao.subtitle: Legacy university extension system modernization: from coupled monolith to clean architecture, tests and observability.
refatoracao_extensao.about_p1: Legacy extension management system with coupled code, no tests and manual deploy. Goal was to refactor without full rewrite (strangler fig): isolate domains, apply SOLID and Clean Architecture and create test suite to enable continuous evolution.
refatoracao_extensao.about_p2: Mapped critical flows (proposal submission, evaluation, certification), broke god classes, introduced use cases, repositories and dependency injection. CI now runs lint, tests and Docker image build on each PR.
refatoracao_extensao.method_p: 1) Characterization tests, 2) Use case extraction, 3) Dependency inversion for repositories, 4) DTOs and validation, 5) Containerization and pipeline. Metrics: cyclomatic complexity -42% and deploy 45min → 6min.
refatoracao_extensao.tech_p: TypeScript/Node or Python, Docker, GitHub Actions, Vitest/Jest, Prisma/TypeORM, ESLint. ADR docs.
refatoracao_extensao.conclusion_p: Refactoring with safety net tests allows fearless evolution. Next: observability with structured logs and metrics. Solid base for Software Architecture course.

ecommerce.title: Gaming E-commerce
ecommerce.subtitle: Full-stack MVC platform with AdonisJS (Node), REST API, ORM, Stripe, wishlist and admin panel — from PC to PS5.
ecommerce.about_p1: Full-stack gaming e-commerce with AdonisJS on NodeJS, following MVC. Backend is REST API with auth, sessions and SQLite via ORM (migrations + seeders). Catalog seeding via RAWG API.
ecommerce.about_p2: Features: user and item CRUD with admin panel, wishlist, comments, persistent cart, debouncing + pagination on search and Stripe gateway.
ecommerce.method_p: Auth + admin, game CRUD, wishlist, 300ms debounce + pagination, Stripe Checkout and webhook.
ecommerce.tech_p: AdonisJS v5, TypeScript, JavaScript, Edge, Lucid ORM, SQLite, HTML/CSS, Stripe JS.
ecommerce.conclusion_p: Full end-to-end project, basis for System Design and deployment studies.

programacao_competitiva.title: Competitive Programming & Algorithms

pesquisa_llm.title: LLMs, Economics and BigFive
pesquisa_llm.subtitle: Thesis research bridging Computing, Economics and Psychology: how BigFive personality and macroeconomic context influence LLM simulated decisions.
pesquisa_llm.about_p1: During my thesis, I developed interdisciplinary research to investigate LLM simulated decision-making under different Big Five personality spectra (Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Neuroticism) and macroeconomic contexts (high inflation, recession, expansion).
pesquisa_llm.about_p2: The lib-teste-bigfive-llm library orchestrates prompts with BigFive-varying personas and measures strategy (e.g., risk propensity, cooperation in prisoner's dilemma).
pesquisa_llm.gallery_desc: BigFive persona, economic games and cooperation heatmap.
pesquisa_llm.gallery_img1_caption: Figure 1 — BigFive trait variation in personas.
pesquisa_llm.gallery_img2_caption: Figure 2 — Ultimatum game simulation by LLMs.
pesquisa_llm.method_p: Persona with BigFive, economic context (9% inflation, tight credit), task (Ultimatum, Investment, risk), LLMs via API, metrics: cooperation rate, avg offer, consistency.
pesquisa_llm.conclusion_p: Agreeableness and Neuroticism had highest impact on cooperation; recession increased risk aversion even in extraverts. Paper in progress.
